paradigm.demoHint: Tabular Q-learning on a maze — educational

deep.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning
deep.intro: Here the agent no longer learns a table but a neural network, able to handle continuous states. Pick an environment (standard Gymnasium, the built-in SOC triage, or your own CSV), one of 13 algorithms, then launch a real training run on CPU — the resulting agents can be saved, re-evaluated, exported and re-imported.
deep.step1Hint: Each environment is a standard control problem with continuous states.
deep.step2Hint: PPO and A2C handle both action types; DQN handles discrete actions only.
deep.step3Hint: Every slider has an AI button to understand — and apply — a good setting.
deep.step4Hint: Learning curve and reward per evaluation episode.
deep.empty: Choose an environment (step 1), an algorithm (step 2), tune it and launch training to see whether the agent learns.
deep.error: Training failed — is the backend running?
deep.cancelled: Training cancelled — the shown results are partial.

verdict.solvedText: The policy beats the solved threshold: the agent has mastered the task.
verdict.unsolvedText: Reward stays below the threshold — try more training steps, or adjust the learning rate.
verdict.doneText: This environment has no official threshold: judge quality from the curve and the mean reward.
verdict.beatsRandomTitle: Useful model — beats the random policy
verdict.beatsRandomText: The learned policy clearly outperforms acting at random (see "Gain vs random"): the agent learned something usable. Use the AI diagnosis for next steps.
verdict.notBetterText: The reward does not beat a random policy: the agent hasn't learned yet. Increase training steps, change algorithm, or revisit the hyperparameters.

total_timesteps.label: Training steps
total_timesteps.hint: Total agent-environment interactions. More = better policy but longer training.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.hint: Gradient-descent step of the network. High = learns fast but unstable; low = slow but stable.

gamma.label: Discount factor (gamma)
gamma.hint: Weight of future rewards: close to 1 = long-term view; lower = favours immediate gain.

ent_coef.label: Entropy coefficient
ent_coef.hint: Encourages exploration by penalising over-confident policies. 0 = no incentive.

exploration_fraction.label: Exploration fraction
exploration_fraction.hint: Share of training over which exploration decays (Deep epsilon-greedy). The counterpart of tabular Q-learning exploration.

tau.label: Soft update (tau)
tau.hint: How fast the target network moves toward the current one. Small = stable but slow target; large = more reactive but unstable.

buffer_size.label: Replay buffer size
buffer_size.hint: Number of past transitions kept in memory for re-learning (replay buffer). Larger = more history but more memory.

delta_std.label: Perturbation scale (delta)
delta_std.hint: Standard deviation of the weight noise used to explore (ARS). Large = broad but noisy exploration; small = fine but slow.

deep.presetsHint: Ready-to-train configurations, cyber-defense oriented. One click loads one — then train and download the agent.

soc_triage_dqn.name: Triage alerts under budget — simple and fast
soc_triage_dqn.desc: Learns which alerts deserve the limited blocks: block real attacks, spare legitimate traffic. The right first agent to train (value-based, DQN).

soc_triage_ppo.name: Triage alerts under budget — robust variant
soc_triage_ppo.desc: The same triage task, with a method that stays stable on ambiguous situations (actor-critic, PPO). Try it when the simple version plateaus.

soc_triage_maskable.name: Triage alerts — budget strictly enforced
soc_triage_maskable.desc: Same triage, but the agent physically cannot block once the budget is spent (action masking). For when the constraint must be guaranteed, not just learned.

incident_ppo.name: Contain an infection before it spreads
incident_ppo.desc: At every step: investigate to firm up the diagnosis, isolate segments, or eradicate. Learns the right moment to act while the infection keeps growing (PPO, long horizon).

threshold_sac.name: Tune the IDS detection threshold online
threshold_sac.desc: Tracks an attack campaign as it ramps up and down, nudging the threshold along the way: limit analyst fatigue (false positives) without missing attacks (SAC).

soc_assign_maskable.name: Dispatch incidents between juniors and seniors
soc_assign_maskable.desc: Learns to save the seniors — scarce but always effective — for severe incidents, and hand the rest to juniors. Assigning an already-busy senior is made impossible (masking).

soc_patch_maskable.name: Prioritize vulnerability patching
soc_patch_maskable.desc: Learns to spend the scarce emergency maintenance windows on the findings genuinely at risk (CVSS, active exploitation, exposure) and schedule the rest.

soc_invest_recurrent.name: Know when to close or escalate an investigation
soc_invest_recurrent.desc: Learns how much evidence to gather before closing or escalating a case — not too early (missed incident), not too late (backlog). Memory-based policy (LSTM) tracks what was already seen.

noc_reroute_dqn.name: Reroute congested traffic — simple and fast
noc_reroute_dqn.desc: Learns to save the spare paths for genuine degradations of critical links, without churning healthy ones. The right first network agent (value-based, DQN).

noc_reroute_maskable.name: Reroute traffic — spare paths guaranteed
noc_reroute_maskable.desc: Same task, but rerouting becomes impossible once the spare paths are exhausted (action masking): the capacity constraint is guaranteed.

noc_capacity_sac.name: Scale network capacity online
noc_capacity_sac.desc: Tracks the diurnal cycle and traffic bursts by adjusting provisioned capacity: serve demand without over-provisioning (cost) or dropping traffic (SLA) (SAC).

cartpole_ppo.name: Teaching reference: balance a pole
cartpole_ppo.desc: The RL "hello world", solved in minutes: ideal to check the training chain and learn to read the curves before the cyber tasks.

pendulum_ppo.name: Reference: first continuous-action task
pendulum_ppo.desc: Swing a pendulum up by modulating torque. To understand continuous actions before the IDS threshold or network capacity (PPO).

pendulum_sac.name: Reference: continuous action, frugal learner
pendulum_sac.desc: The same pendulum, with the algorithm that learns from few trials (SAC) — the one used for the continuous cyber and network tasks.

pendulum_crossq.name: Reference: continuous action, recent variant
pendulum_crossq.desc: Still the pendulum, with CrossQ, often even more frugal than SAC. Useful to compare two algorithms on an identical task.

AlertTriage-v0.label: SOC alert triage
AlertTriage-v0.desc: Triage a stream of security alerts under a response budget: each alert (threat score, asset criticality, source reputation, remaining budget) calls for a decision — dismiss, monitor or block. Blocking a real attack pays off; blocking legitimate traffic costs; missing an attack is expensive.

IncidentContainment-v0.label: Incident containment
IncidentContainment-v0.desc: Contain a spreading incident (worm, ransomware lateral movement). The state evolves: the infected fraction grows every step. Investigate (raise confidence), isolate segments (slows the spread but costs the business) or eradicate (expensive, and effective only once the diagnosis is confident). A genuine temporal trade-off.

ThresholdTuning-v0.label: IDS threshold tuning
ThresholdTuning-v0.desc: Continuously tune an IDS detection threshold while an attack campaign ramps up and down. The action is a real number (nudge the threshold). Reward: true positives paid, false positives (analyst fatigue) and missed attacks charged — the exact trade-off of the supervised threshold panel, but online.

AnalystAssignment-v0.label: SOC analyst assignment
AnalystAssignment-v0.desc: Dispatch a queue of incidents to a limited team: defer, assign a junior or a senior. Seniors always resolve but stay busy for several steps; juniors fail on hard incidents (costly rework); deferring a severe incident gets more and more expensive. The resource-allocation trade-off a SOC shift lead faces.

PatchPrioritization-v0.label: Patch prioritization
PatchPrioritization-v0.desc: Prioritize a queue of vulnerabilities under a maintenance-window budget: each finding (CVSS score, active exploitation à la KEV catalogue, internet exposure, remaining windows) calls for a decision — defer, schedule for the next cycle, or patch in an emergency window. Emergency-patching a vulnerability about to be exploited pays off; burning a window (production disruption) on a benign finding is wasteful; deferring a vulnerability that then gets exploited is very expensive.

CaseInvestigation-v0.label: Case investigation
CaseInvestigation-v0.desc: Decide when to stop investigating a suspicious case (optimal stopping). The truth is hidden: the agent only sees a noisy suspicion estimate. Investigating costs analyst time and inflates the backlog but pulls the estimate toward the truth; closing a real incident is very costly; escalating a benign case wastes incident response. Partially observable — a recurrent policy (RecurrentPPO) has a genuine edge.

TrafficRerouting-v0.label: NOC traffic rerouting
TrafficRerouting-v0.desc: Handle a stream of congestion events under a spare-path budget: each event (utilization, latency, link criticality, remaining budget) calls for a decision — keep, throttle or reroute. Rerouting a genuine degradation pays off; rerouting a healthy link churns flows for nothing; ignoring a degradation is expensive.

CapacityScaling-v0.label: Capacity scaling
CapacityScaling-v0.desc: Continuously adjust provisioned capacity while demand follows a diurnal cycle with random bursts. The action is a real number (scale capacity up or down). Reward: served traffic paid, over-provisioning charged (cost), dropped traffic heavily charged (SLA) — the classic NOC dimensioning trade-off, online.

CartPole-v1.label: CartPole
CartPole-v1.desc: Keep an inverted pole balanced by moving a cart left or right.

Acrobot-v1.label: Acrobot
Acrobot-v1.desc: Swing an underactuated double pendulum to raise its tip above a line.

MountainCar-v0.label: MountainCar
MountainCar-v0.desc: Build momentum to drive an underpowered car up a hill.

Pendulum-v1.label: Pendulum
Pendulum-v1.desc: Apply continuous torque to swing up and stabilise a pendulum upright.

MountainCarContinuous-v0.label: MountainCar (continuous)
MountainCarContinuous-v0.desc: Continuous-action version of MountainCar: precisely modulate the push.

envs.customDesc: SOC triage environment built from your imported CSV ({{n}} alerts). The agent learns to triage on your real data.

PPO.desc: Robust and versatile, the default choice. Handles discrete and continuous actions.

DQN.desc: The Deep counterpart of tabular Q-learning. Discrete actions only.

A2C.desc: Simpler, faster cousin of PPO. Handles both action types.

SAC.desc: Maximum-entropy off-policy, very sample-efficient. The best default for continuous control. Continuous actions only.

TD3.desc: Twin-critic off-policy, stabilises deterministic learning. Continuous actions only.

DDPG.desc: Deterministic off-policy actor-critic, the predecessor of TD3. Continuous actions only.

QRDQN.desc: Distributional DQN: learns the distribution of returns, not just their mean. Discrete actions only (sb3-contrib).

TRPO.desc: Trust-region optimisation: bounded updates for stability. Discrete and continuous actions (sb3-contrib).

TQC.desc: Truncated quantile critics, curbs value overestimation. Often beats SAC on continuous control (sb3-contrib).

RecurrentPPO.desc: Recurrent PPO (LSTM): keeps a memory of past observations, useful for partially observable states. Discrete and continuous actions (sb3-contrib).

ARS.desc: Augmented Random Search: optimises the policy without gradients, very simple and robust. A good counterpoint to gradient methods. Discrete and continuous actions (sb3-contrib).

CrossQ.desc: Off-policy continuous control without target networks (BatchNorm), often more sample-efficient than SAC. Continuous actions only (sb3-contrib).

MaskablePPO.desc: PPO with action masking: forbids invalid actions given the state (e.g. blocking when the SOC budget is spent). Maskable environments only (sb3-contrib).

deep.evalText: These results measure a previously trained agent's policy, without retraining — so the learning curve is empty.

intro.title: Reinforcement learning
intro.body: No fixed dataset here: an <0>agent</0> learns by trial and error while interacting with an <1>environment</1> — a <2> GridWorld</2> maze in this case. At each step it picks an action, receives a<3> reward</3>, and adjusts its strategy (<4>Q-learning</4>) to maximize cumulative reward. It starts from cell <5>S</5> and must reach a goal by the shortest path, avoiding traps.

diagram.ariaLabel: Agent-environment loop: the agent acts, the environment answers with a state and a reward

discovery.name: Discovery
discovery.desc: Small empty world: the ideal convergence.

maze.name: Maze
maze.desc: Walls to navigate around to find the exit.

board.stepDesc: Pick a tool then click the grid to build the world.
board.autoNoteSuffix: placed automatically during training — visible on the grid afterwards.

size.label: Grid size
size.hint: Side of the N×N maze — bigger = more states to explore.

n_goals.label: Number of goals
n_goals.hint: Goal cells (goals beyond the bottom-right corner are placed at random).

n_traps.label: Random traps
n_traps.hint: Traps added at random, on top of hand-placed ones.

episodes.label: Number of episodes
episodes.hint: Training games: the more there are, the better the Q table converges.

alpha.label: Learning rate (α)
alpha.hint: Speed of the Q update: high = fast but unstable.

gamma.label: Discount factor (γ)
gamma.hint: Weight of the future: close to 1 = long-term strategy.

epsilon.label: Initial exploration (ε)
epsilon.hint: Share of random actions at the start, which decays over episodes.

panel.stepDesc: Every slider has an AI button to understand — and apply — a good setting.

results.stepDesc: Reward curve, learned policy and value function.
results.staleMessage: Configuration changed since this run — these results describe the previous run. Restart training to refresh them.
results.emptyHint: Build the world (step 1), tune the algorithm (step 2), then launch training to see whether the agent learns to reach the goal.

success.title: The agent has learned
success.text: It reaches a goal in {{rate}}% of the last episodes: the policy has converged.

partial.title: Partial learning
partial.text: The policy is progressing but stays fragile — try more episodes, or a lower α to stabilize.

fail.title: The agent has not converged
fail.text: Too few episodes, too hostile a world, or poorly tuned exploration: adjust and rerun.

errors.trainFailedNoBackend: Training failed — is the backend running?

outcome.stuck: stuck (the policy pushes into a wall).
outcome.loop: endless loop — the policy did not converge here.
